Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis: Viral gastroenteritis (acute infectious gastroenteritis), likely viral etiology given abrupt onset of watery diarrhea, initial vomiting, feverish sensation, absence of blood in stool, and recent takeout exposure.
- Supporting considerations from DDx (consistent with transcript findings): 
  - Bacterial gastroenteritis/food poisoning (possible due to takeout food 4 days prior to symptoms). 
  - Post-infectious lactose intolerance/osmotic diarrhea or less likely IBD flare (left-lower quadrant cramps after GI illness; less likely without prior history).
  - Giardia or other parasitic enteritis considered but less likely given rapid acute course.
- Plan:
  - Conservative management with hydration and symptomatic care; no antibiotics indicated at this time.
  - Oral rehydration: Dioralyte or equivalent to replenish fluids/electrolytes.
  - Symptom relief: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) as needed for fever/weakness; dose/frequency not documented.
  - Work and activity: Recommend taking 2–3 days off work to rest as infection clears.
  - Monitoring: If symptoms persist or worsen, return for re-evaluation in 3–4 days; stool sample considered if symptoms persist to identify infectious etiology.
  - Education: Emphasize hydration, gradual reintroduction of bland foods, and warning signs requiring urgent care (dehydration, high fever, persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids down).
- Considerations:
  - If no improvement within 3–4 days, broaden evaluation for other etiologies (e.g., bacterial gastroenteritis, parasitic infection) and consider stool testing.
  - No antibiotic therapy unless a bacterial etiology is confirmed or strongly suspected.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Hydration strategies, oral rehydration solution use, recognition of dehydration and return precautions; avoid unnecessary antibiotic use.
- Patient health goals and priorities: Recovery from acute GI illness with restoration of normal activity; maintain hydration; resume work when well.
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): Stool testing referral if persistent symptoms; follow-up appointment if symptoms persist or worsen.
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Reassess in 3–4 days if not improved; earlier if worsening.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Viral gastroenteritis
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Acute onset of watery diarrhea with initial vomiting, feverish sensation, no blood in stool, and recent food exposure; consistent with a viral gastroenteritis pattern.
- Bacterial gastroenteritis/food poisoning (e.g., Salmonella, Campylobacter)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Takeout meal 4 days prior with subsequent diarrhea and cramping; incubation can fit certain pathogens.
- Post-infectious lactose intolerance / IBD flare
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Left-lower quadrant cramps and diarrhea after GI illness; absence of prior IBD history makes active IBD less likely, lactose intolerance possible but not documented.

- Giardia or other parasitic enteritis
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Diarrhea with cramps; possible but less likely given rapid acute course.

- Internal conflicts or contradictions between transcript and DDx: None identified; fever described as feverish sensation but no objective fever measurement provided.
- Transcript quality notes: Not all exam findings or vitals documented; relies on patient report for symptoms and clinical impression.
